panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial chest CT demonstrating bronchiectasis, a hallmark radiological finding of Kartagener syndrome. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a real human patient bronchoscopy image showing mirror-image tracheobronchial anatomy consistent with situs inversus totalis, a defining clinical manifestation of Kartagener syndrome as described in the associated article. B: Panel B is a real human patient bronchoscopy image demonstrating reversed left bronchial branching (three lobar branches) with an arrow highlighting segmental branches, confirming mirror-image anatomy consistent with situs inversus totalis, a key feature of Kartagener syndrome. C: Panel C is a real human patient bronchoscopy image showing reversed right bronchial branching (two lobar branches) consistent with mirror-image anatomy of situs inversus totalis, a defining manifestation of Kartagener syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Hazarika et al. Adequacy of Clinical and Radiological Evidence for the Management of Kartagener Syndrome.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.91091. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Bronchoscopy. Flexible bronchoscopy of the tracheobronchial tree revealed mirror-image anatomy consistent with situs inversus. Panel A shows the tracheal bifurcation at the carina, with clear visualization of the right and left main bronchi. Panel B demonstrates the left main bronchus, which in situs inversus gives rise to three lobar branches (upper, middle, and lower). The red arrow in panel B highlights the segmental branches arising from the left middle lobe bronchus (B4–B5), along with the superior segment branch (S6) and basal branches (B7–B10), thereby confirming mirror-image anatomy. Panel C shows the right main bronchus dividing into two lobar branches (upper and lower), analogous to the branching pattern of the physiological left lung, further validating reversed bronchial anatomy.
